 Pasco County couple waits months for $24k tax refund
 Shannon Behnken Updated 2026년 10월 29일 목 오후 11:54 UTC 0 TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA) — A Pasco County couple has been waiting since February for a $24,851 income tax refund. 
 After months of delays, repeated requests for information and little explanation, they called Better Call Behnken for help.
[sailthru_widget name="Sailthru Widget Block" sailthru_list="8 on Your Side" title="8 on Your Side"]
 Cathy Boucher said she and her husband intentionally have more taxes withheld than necessary because they enjoy receiving a refund. 
 This year, they were surprised when their accountant informed them they were owed $24,851.
 “We were in a transition period, and I definitely went to a different tax bracket,” Boucher said. “And I over-withheld both on an IRA withdrawal and also on my W2 withholding.”
 Clearwater church out $736K after contractor uses funds for vehicle, vacations: CPD 
 The couple filed their taxes in mid-February. 
 In March, they were asked to verify their identities. Boucher said they were initially told it would take nine weeks to receive their refund. Later, they were told to expect a 180-day wait.
 But the money never arrived, and the couple struggled to get answers about what was causing the delay.
 Advertisement
 “I don't know, is there an error and we just need to do an amended return?” Boucher said. “Or my biggest fear was that somebody filed under our Social Security numbers and that there really was an identity theft problem.”
 Although receiving the refund is important, Boucher said the uncertainty has been just as troubling.
 “Our biggest concern, yes, we would like our refund, but it's the not knowing what's happening,” she said.
 Last month, Boucher applied for help from a taxpayer advocate. She was assigned a case number but was told the process could result in another 90-day wait.
 With no clear resolution in sight, the couple contacted Better Call Behnken in hopes of getting answers and moving the case forward.
 “So right now, we're still in a holding pattern and just trying to figure out if there's a way to get an answer,” Boucher said.
 For the couple, the issue goes beyond the money.
 “It's not just the money, but is there something wrong? And if there is, what is it? So we can fix it,” Boucher said.
 A spokesperson for the IRS tells Better Call Behnken they have escalated the issue to the taxpayer advocate office and that office has now reached out to the couple.
 Better Call Behnken will stay on this story until it is fully resolved.
